column3: NASB renders “toward” as “against.”
NASB renders “of the way” as “belonging to the Way.”
NASB follows the critical text; it renders “in the proceeding” as “as he journeyed.”
NASB renders “do you persecute” as “are you persecuting.”
NASB follows the critical text without “It is hard for you to kick against the goads.”
NASB follows the critical text without the Textus Receptus words “trembling and astonished he said, Lord, what will You have me do?” A stray quotation mark appears in the NASB text.
Close to the Greek.
NASB follows the critical text; it adds “though.”
NASB renders “without seeing” as “without sight.”
NASB renders “Behold me” as “Behold, here am I.”
NASB adds “a man”; “seek” is rendered “inquire.”
NASB follows the critical text; “saw” is rendered “has seen,” and “see again” is “regain his sight.”
NASB follows the critical text; “how many evils” is rendered “how much harm.”
Close to the Greek.
NASB follows the critical text; “a vessel of choice” is rendered “a chosen instrument.”
NASB adds “sake.”
NASB reorders the verse and renders “see again” as “regain your sight.”
NASB follows the critical text; it adds “something like.”
NASB follows the critical text without “Saul”; it moves “for several days” earlier.
NASB follows the critical text (“Jesus”); it adds “saying.”
NASB follows the critical text; “caused havoc” is rendered “destroyed.”
NASB adds “Jesus” to “this.”
NASB renders “execute” as “do away with.”
NASB follows the critical text.
NASB follows the critical text (“his disciples”); it adds “an opening in” and “large.”
NASB follows the critical text without “Saul”; “join” is rendered “associate.”
NASB renders “having taken” as “took hold of.”
NASB follows the critical text with “the Lord” (no “Jesus”); it moves “speaking boldly,” which opens v. 29 in the Greek, into this verse.
NASB follows the critical text; “Hellenists” is rendered “Hellenistic Jews.”
NASB renders “brothers” as “brethren.”
